survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS/PIAAC) and therefore does not implement a sampling design, plausible-value scaling, or survey-weighted estimation. The document describes governance and stakeholder responsibilities for Latvia’s adult skills system across national and subnational levels (ministries, agencies, municipalities, and providers). As a result, there are no student-level weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) to apply. Any weighting guidance that would normally be relevant for ILSA achievement analyses is not applicable to this policy/governance description.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a governance and policy country note describing institutional responsibilities in Latvia’s adult skills system, not an empirical analysis of student achievement or other cognitive outcomes. Because there is no ILSA-style dependent variable based on cognitive test items, plausible values (PV-based achievement scores) are not applicable. Similarly, there is no missing-data handling procedure reported because no student-level dataset, item responses, or analytic sample are constructed in the note.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used no ILSA microdata; the note provides a qualitative/administrative overview of Latvia’s adult skills governance structure and responsibilities at national and local levels.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Latvia country note summarizes how adult skills systems are governed, focusing on the division of responsibilities across national ministries/agencies and subnational municipalities. It reports structural information such as the degree of centralisation, the role of municipalities in non-formal CET/AE provision, and the oversight of ALMPs through the Ministry of Welfare and the State Employment Agency with deconcentrated local offices. The note includes tables mapping responsibilities across policy areas (strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, delivery) and describes stakeholder roles (social partners, expert councils, VET/HVET providers). No ILSA assessment data, student sampling, test scaling, or predictive modeling is conducted, so there are no ML performance metrics or achievement benchmarks to interpret. The implication is policy-oriented: strengthening coordination mechanisms between national agencies and municipalities may improve access and relevance of adult learning and employment services.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the document is not an empirical large-scale assessment study: it is a policy/governance country note without an analytic sample, measurement model, or ML pipeline. Consequently, fields such as total_students, country-level student counts, PV handling, missing-data handling, and ML findings are not applicable to the document’s purpose.
